content.thinking:
The deploy timing lines up exactly with the onset—the new code changed average_spend_per_item into an O(n²) loop that recomputes the sum for each index instead of doing it once, which explains the latency spike seen in the p50, p95, and p99 numbers.

CPU usage stayed flat around 0.75, far below the limit, so this isn't resource exhaustion—it's purely a computation-heavy inefficiency that hits harder for accounts with many purchases. The error rate barely moved, and those client disconnects look like shoppers timing out from the slowness rather than a separate issue, so everything points to a bad code deployment rather than a config problem, and I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.

hypotheses.subject: src/io_shop/spend_summary.py (average_spend_per_item)
hypotheses.summary: The 07:03:00Z deploy of revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655 changed average_spend_per_item to recompute the running total from scratch for every purchase (an O(n^2) loop) instead of using the account's carried total. This made the account-page rendering path far slower per request, which lines up exactly with the onset of the latency spike (p50 44ms->262ms->460ms, p95 220ms->1268ms->2130ms, p99 383ms->2093ms->3870ms) starting at 07:03:00Z, the same minute as the deploy. The elevated errors seen in the logs are ClientDisconnected - shoppers timing out/giving up while the now-slow account page renders - consistent with a latency-caused failure rather than a downstream dependency failing outright.
